title: Comparative patterns of ultraviolet-induced visible response in bat wing membranes across families and trophic guilds
content:
Abstract
Photoluminescence has been documented in several mammalian taxa, yet its occurrence and potential significance in bats remain poorly understood. We present a comparative assessment of ultraviolet-induced visible response (UV-IVR), a form of UV-excited photoluminescence, in 97 bat species from eight families. Museum specimens were examined under 365- and 395-nm UV excitation to evaluate UV-IVR in external structures (pelage and wing membranes) and internal structures (blood vessels and skeletal elements, including phalanges). External UV-IVR was widespread under 395-nm excitation but was rarely detected under 365-nm excitation. In contrast, internal structures, particularly blood vessels and phalanges, were frequently visible at both wavelengths. Marked family-level differences were observed: Molossidae exhibited strong external UV-IVR with little internal visibility, Vespertilionidae showed the highest vascular visibility, and Phyllostomidae displayed intermediate patterns with greater skeletal than vascular visibility. Trophic guilds also differed, with arthropodophagous taxa showing greater vascular visibility and frugivores greater skeletal visibility. These results indicate that UV-IVR in bats varies across lineages and ecological guilds and is strongly wavelength-dependent in external structures, whereas internal structures remain broadly detectable across excitation wavelengths. Further studies are needed to determine whether these responses have functional or signalling roles.
